newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No progress in Israel-PLO talks, Ross going home.
newsitem.headline: No progress in Israel-PLO talks, Ross going home.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross will return to Washington on Monday after Israel and the PLO failed to clinch a deal on a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron, officials on both sides said.

"There were no achievements and no agreement. Ross is going back to the United States," said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak. A PLO negotiator said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had left Gaza for Europe.
Bazak accused the Palestinians of stalling in talks overnight and said the agreement could have been sealed had Arafat given his consent.
Palestinians have said Israel was trying to renegotiate terms of the Hebron withdrawal which the Jewish state agreed to more than a year ago.

"Palestinian and Israeli negotiators failed to agree. Talks ended very early this morning without any agreement on the same issues," said Palestinian negotiator Hassan Asfour. "Arafat has already left," he said.

U.S. President Bill Clinton telephoned both Netanyahu and Arafat on Sunday to urge them to conclude the agreement and Ross had said Arafat's departure on a European tour would hamper his mediation efforts.
